title: He must be at home
goal: Make a confident guess with -dYr, and follow family news told with -(Y)pdYr and eken.

intro.text: `-dYr` often marks a guess: *Ol öýdedir*, he must be at home. After verbs: *Ol eýýäm gelendir* (he must have arrived), *Ol uklaýandyr* (he must be sleeping), *Ol ertir geljekdir* (he'll probably come tomorrow). *megerem* and *ähtimal* mean **probably**.

exercises.question: Merdan always gets home at six. It's seven now, and you're at work. What do you say?

why.1: *gelipdir* rests on evidence: you saw his shoes, or someone told you.
why.2: *geldi* says you know it for a fact.

exercises.explain: A confident guess from what usually happens: *gelendir*, he must have come.

exercises.en: He's not answering his phone. He must be sleeping.

reject.why: *uklaýar* states it as a fact. You're guessing: *uklaýandyr*.
*uklapdyr* means you know it from evidence or from someone. A guess: *uklaýandyr*.

exercises.explain: *ukla-* + *-ýan* + *-dyr*: he must be sleeping. (*uklandyr*, he must have fallen asleep, fits too.)

reject.why: *Sen ýadaw* states it: **you're tired**. A guess: *ýadawdyrsyň*.

exercises.explain: `-dYr` with the ending of **you**: *ýadaw-dyr-syň*, you must be tired.

exercises.label: *gelmek*: he'll probably come, they'll probably come
exercises.explain: `-jAk` + `-dYr`: *geljekdir*, a guess about what will happen.
*git-* softens before the vowel of *-en*; then *-dir*: *gidendir*.

exercises.title: Obadan täzelik
exercises.passage:
Düýn agşam ejäm obadaky daýym bilen telefonda gürleşdi. Soňra ol bize täzelikleri gürrüň berdi. Daýymyň uly ogly Batyr öýlenipdir! Toý geçen hepde bolupdyr. Gelin daşoguzly eken, ol mugallym bolup işleýän eken. Indi olar Aşgabada göçjek eken.

Kakam geň galdy: “Batyr bize näme üçin jaň etmedi?” Ejäm güldi: “Megerem, ol örän meşguldyr. Ýa-da ol bizi ýatdan çykarandyr!” Kakam ertir Batyra jaň etjek.
exercises.translation: Last night my mother talked on the phone with my uncle in the village. Then she told us the news. My uncle's elder son Batyr has got married! The wedding was last week, it seems. The bride is from Dashoguz, it turns out, and she works as a teacher. Now they're going to move to Ashgabat, we hear. My father was surprised: “Why didn't Batyr call us?” My mother laughed: “He must be very busy. Or he must have forgotten us!” My father is going to call Batyr tomorrow.

questions.q: How did the family hear the news?
options: Mum spoke to the uncle on the phone.
questions.explain: *ejäm obadaky daýym bilen telefonda gürleşdi*: the phone call is something they saw, so `-dY`.

questions.q: Why are the wedding and Batyr's marriage told with *bolupdyr* and *öýlenipdir*?
options: The family only heard about them.
The family was at the wedding.
questions.explain: `-(Y)pdYr` passes on what they heard; the details about the bride come with *eken*.

questions.q: What does *Megerem, ol örän meşguldyr* say?
options: a guess: he must be very busy
a fact: he is very busy
questions.explain: *megerem* and `-dYr`: Mum is guessing why Batyr didn't call.

exercises.explain: `-jAk` + `-dYr` for a guess about the future; `-Ar` also says **probably will** ([A2 unit 4](a2-u04)).

exercises.prompt: Aýna öýde däldir. Onuň maşyny bu ýerde ýok.
accept: Aýna probably isn't at home. Her car isn't here.
Aýna [probably isn't home|must not be at home|can't be at home|isn't at home, I guess]. Her car isn't here.
Aýna can't be home. Her car isn't here.

exercises.question: Merdan isn't answering the phone. Which sentence is a guess?

why.1: *gitdi*: you know he went, maybe you saw him leave.
why.2: *gidipdir*: you know it from someone, or from what you see.

exercises.explain: *işdedir*, he must be at work: `-dYr` for a confident guess.

exercises.text: You must be tired, sit down.
